title: Flock Safety registry records (December 2025 snapshot) confirmed removed by 21 October 2026
registry: flocksurveillance.org (Michael 2026): Flock Safety's device records as of December 2025; record ids as in its device list
how: Two kinds of evidence. 'news': the operating agency, or the press reporting it, says the readers were removed; each place's in-service registry records were matched to the agency by their labels and counts (the notes say where a count or an identity is uncertain). 'osm_deletion': the OpenStreetMap node paired with the record in September 2026 was deleted with a comment saying the camera was removed (the changeset is the source). Sources checked 2026-10-22.

places.note: KATV gives no count; the city removed all of its cameras, and the registry has two in service there.
places.evidence: "The city of Mayflower has announced that they have removed all of their Flock cameras and terminated services with the company."
"The City received confirmation on Feb. 19 that all Flock Safety cameras covered under the City's contract have been physically removed."
KTVU: all 40 cameras offline since June; Flock removed the last of them two days before the shooting of 23 Aug.
Santa Cruz Local: as of 9 March all eight cameras in Santa Cruz were removed.
places.note: The page refused our fetch; verified from its indexed text.

places.evidence: "A Colorado sheriff's department took matters into its own hands earlier this month, dismantling 10 Flock license plate reader cameras after it said Flock Safety would not come to remove them as asked."
"Seminole County Sheriff's Office officials said all of the department's Flock cameras and attached solar panels have been removed."
"In September, the St. Johns County Sheriff's Office removed 84 LPRs in accordance with the Florida Department of Transportation's directive to remove LPRs on state rights-of-way."

Tampa Police: "All of our ALPRs located within the right-of-way of a road on the State Highway System have been removed in compliance with FDOT notice" (17 readers; the city's 1 Sept statement set the 30-day timeline).
places.note: Our 3 records are the in-service readers among the 17 whose registry labels name a state road.

places.evidence: "…before swiftly removing them this week after the RoundTable requested comment on their presence."
City memo dated 2026-10-07: "all existing ALPRs have already been removed and the ALPR Flock contract canceled".
places.note: No count or removal date given; the 11 are the city's fixed readers. The memo implies its Flex and trailer units are gone too; we did not drop those.

places.evidence: "The city confirms the four cameras near Holly Lane have already been removed."
"On Thursday morning, deputy police chief Charlie Gibson was spotted removing the cameras in a bucket truck"
"Stow has also canceled its contract with Flock and removed three cameras that had previously been installed, officials said."
"…as of June 22, 2026, Flock confirmed all cameras have been removed and there is no active South Portland account."
"…despite ending usage of the tools (removing flexible-location cameras and covering fixed-location cameras with black trash bags)…"
"All six have been physically removed and are in the process of being returned to Flock Safety."
"All county cameras have been removed as of Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026."
FOX 9: all eight of the city's Flock cameras were stolen (poles cut down) and none had been recovered by 4 Aug.
places.note: Stolen, not taken down by the city; no report of replacement by 21 Oct.

places.evidence: Town of Hillsborough: as of 3 Dec 2025 all Flock Safety cameras contracted by the town have been removed.
places.note: The page refused our fetch; verified from its indexed text.
13 removed, as reported; a photo shows an East Adams St reader removed on 14 July, and the registry's only in-service one there (#25) is the one we kept, so one of our 13 may be the wrong record.
places.evidence: "The company on Wednesday confirmed that it had removed all of its 13 license plate readers from city property."
"…after four out of the city's six cameras were stolen a few weeks ago, the police department took the last two down."
"The city announced Thursday that staff removed all cameras under Liberty Hill's Flock program on Tuesday, Sept. 15."
ARLnow: all county-leased Flock technology removed (26 Falcon plate readers and 15 Condor PTZ cameras).
places.note: 27 records against the 26 readers ARLnow counts; one, F#012 just inside Alexandria or LR#031, may not be the county's.
The sheriff removed them 'while we continue to evaluate', so they could return.
places.evidence: "Augusta County Sheriff Donald Smith says two were removed on Friday, September 25, that were operating on Jefferson Highway."
"The Town of Christiansburg has removed all but one of its Flock cameras, officials announced in a Facebook post Wednesday."
Northern Virginia Daily: Public Works staff took down the city's Flock readers after the contract ended on 31 July (31 cameras).
places.note: The page rate-limited our fetch; verified from its indexed text.

places.evidence: "A resident contacted him today and said one camera remains on Commerce Road."
